subject: Subprocessor inventory, Art.28/30 records & DPIA inputs — request from CloudRetail
messages:
From: Katie Summers <katie.summers@cloudretail.com>
To: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-09-01T09:12:00-04:00
Subject: Information request: subprocessors / Art. 28 & 30 records for DPIA

Hi Diego —

As part of our procurement/privacy review for the upcoming pilot, Legal asked us to collect a few items so we can complete our DPIA and Art. 28 review:

- A current list of all subprocessors (name, subprocessor role, country/region, access type) in spreadsheet form (we prefer .xlsx).
- A copy or summary of your Art. 30 processing records for services relevant to CloudRetail (data categories, purposes, retention).
- Evidence of lawful transfer mechanisms for EU data (SCCs, adequacy decisions, or DPF where applicable).
- Any DPIA notes or mitigations that mention our use case (embedding/search + customer PII handling).
- Confirmation whether any subprocessors have access to plaintext customer data, and if so, what controls are in place (encryption, ACLs, contractual constraints, access auditing).

Would you be able to provide these artifacts within two weeks? If you have a consolidated DPA/DOCUSIGN link that covers SCCs and subprocessors, please include it.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Katie Summers
Senior Privacy Manager
CloudRetail Ltd

From: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-09-01T09:40:00-04:00
Subject: Fwd: Information request: subprocessors / Art. 28 & 30 records for DPIA

Laura / Monica —

Forwarding CloudRetail's request (below). They want a subprocessor inventory, Art. 30 register, evidence of transfer mechanisms, and DPIA-relevant notes. Can you assemble the artifacts and confirm whether we need any new vendor attestations for this account?

Quick facts for context: pilot will process EU customer data; CloudRetail asked about plaintext access by subprocessors. We currently host EU tenant data in eu-west-1 by default and use SCCs for transfers where required.

Attachments: CloudRetail_RFP_20250901.pdf (their RFP brief)

Timeline: they asked for two weeks, but if we can turn around in ~3 business days that would be ideal.

Thanks —
Diego
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-09-02T14:05:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Information request: subprocessors / Art. 28 & 30 records for DPIA

Diego —

Thanks for the heads up. I pulled together the artifacts we can share immediately. High-level summary below; attached are the working files.

What I'm sending (attached):
- subprocessors_list_20250902.xlsx — inventory with role, location, access type, and last vetting date.
- redwood_art30_processing_register_20250902.pdf — processing activities relevant to the platform and retention windows.
- redwood_scc_evidence_20250902.pdf — copy of our SCC addendum + execution guidance we rely on for EU transfers.
- notes: internal DPIA brief (internal only) — we should not publish this to external without redaction.

Key points to call out for CloudRetail:
- Transfer mechanism: for EU data we rely primarily on the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (Module II/III as applicable). We also host customer workloads in region-specific clusters (eu-west-1) to avoid unnecessary cross-border flows.
- Subprocessors: most are SaaS infra providers (monitoring, observability) that only receive aggregated/metric telemetry. Two service providers (a logging vendor and a managed dataset indexing vendor) have limited access to customer tokens/indices under strict contractual and technical controls.
- Plaintext access: by default, customer data is encrypted at rest and in transit. Only named subprocessors with justified business need have any capacity to access plaintext; access is logged, role-based, and subject to quarterly access reviews. We will include a per-subprocessor statement on plaintext access in the inventory spreadsheet under the "access_type" column.
- DPIA support: we can provide a short memo mapping Redwood mitigations to common DPIA risk categories (data minimization, encryption, access controls, retention). That memo is internal — Monica, can you produce a redacted external version for CloudRetail?

Next steps:
- Monica: produce a redacted DPIA memo (external-facing) + confirm per-subprocessor plaintext access fields.
- Rishi: confirm the most recent SCC execution record and whether any subprocessors are located in jurisdictions requiring additional controls.
- Diego: I'll hand you the finalized artifacts for outbound to CloudRetail; please don't attach the internal DPIA memo.

Laura Bennett
Head of Legal
Redwood Inference

From: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Katie Summers <katie.summers@cloudretail.com>, legal@cloudretail.com
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-09-03T10:22:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Information request: subprocessors / Art. 28 & 30 records for DPIA

Hi Katie —

Thanks for the clear list. Please find attached the items we can share today:

- subprocessors_list_20250902.xlsx (attached) — inventory with roles, regions, and an "access_type" column that explicitly states whether a subprocessor can access plaintext customer data.
- redwood_art30_processing_register_20250902.pdf (attached) — our Art. 30-style processing register for the services used by CloudRetail.
- redwood_scc_evidence_20250902.pdf (attached) — executed SCC addendum we apply; includes the signed annex template.
- dpa_docusign_20250903.pdf (attached) — DocuSign link included below for the standard DPA we use with enterprise customers.

DocuSign (DPA): https://na2.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?PowerFormId=abc-123

A few targeted clarifications based on Laura's review:
- Hosting & transfers: Cloud customer workloads can be pinned to eu-west-1; when pinned, we do not route or store data outside the region except for transient processing under SCC protections.
- Plaintext access: two named subprocessors ("LogStream Co." and "IndexWorks Ltd") have scoped, audited access to indices/trace data for operational purposes. Both are contractually prevented from using data for ML training or marketing. All access is logged and reviewed quarterly. These details are in the spreadsheet.
- DPIA support: Monica will provide an external-facing DPIA mapping memo that summarizes mitigations for encryption, retention, access control, and model outputs.

If this looks good, can you confirm whether the SCC evidence and inventory are sufficient for Legal, or if you'd like the redacted DPIA memo as well? We can also set up a 30-minute sync with Laura/Monica if you prefer.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

From: Katie Summers <katie.summers@cloudretail.com>
To: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@cloudretail.com
Date: 2025-09-09T15:02:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Information request: subprocessors / Art. 28 & 30 records for DPIA

Diego —

Received, and thank you — the inventory and Art.30 register are very helpful. A couple of follow-ups before Legal can sign off:

1) Can you provide an explicit, signed statement from Redwood confirming the two subprocessors named (LogStream Co. and IndexWorks Ltd) do not use customer data for ML training and that contractual clauses preventing such use are currently in force?

2) For our DPIA we also need a short, external-facing section that states whether any subprocessors have the ability to access plaintext customer PII, and if so, the exact technical controls (e.g., envelope encryption, KMS role separation, logging/retention of access events) — the spreadsheet notes this, but Legal prefers a single-paragraph statement they can reference.

If you can get those two items to us this week, I expect Legal to complete review quickly and we can proceed to countersign the DPA.

Thanks —
Katie Summers
Senior Privacy Manager
CloudRetail Ltd
